subject: Food Science
title: MSG Is Safe
description: A fast breakdown of MSG Is Safe for builders.

hook.text: 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' was coined in 1968 from one anecdotal letter. Decades of research have debunked it entirely.

buildup.text: MSG (monosodium glutamate) is a sodium salt of glutamate—the same amino acid in tomatoes, Parmesan, and breast milk.

discovery.text: Double-blind studies show no difference between MSG and placebo. People who 'react' can't identify it in controlled tests.

twist.text: Restaurant meals have more glutamate from natural sources than from MSG. Soy sauce, mushrooms, and aged cheese contribute more.

climax.text: The FDA, WHO, and EFSA classify MSG as safe. The original 'Chinese Restaurant Syndrome' paper had zero scientific evidence.

punchline.text: MSG fear: one letter, zero evidence, decades of bias. Science says it's safe.

quiz.question: What do controlled studies show about MSG sensitivity?
options: People who claim sensitivity can't distinguish MSG from placebo in blind tests
